problems.description: When direct analytic/Newton-based UV inversion for a 3D point either isn't available for the surface type, lands in a C0-continuity knot region (where derivatives are unreliable), fails to converge, or converges to a worse result than an alternative, the surface analysis falls back through a chain: skip Newton near C0 B-spline knots (evaluate via the general path instead); after Extrema-based search, retry with Newton if the residual exceeds precision and accept it only if it improves on the Extrema result; if that is still unsatisfying (or Extrema found nothing), search along boundary and through-point iso-parametric curves (UVFromIso) and iterate; and if the whole procedure throws (e.g. on an ill-defined offset surface), catch the exception and fall back to the domain midpoint rather than propagating garbage.

problems.description: When a derived/split edge's 3D curve and pcurve parametrizations are not guaranteed synchronized (BRep_Tool::SameParameter()==false, or projection is being forced), each transferred knot's new parameter is chosen between a cheap linear-interpolated value and a true geometric projection, based on which has the smaller 3D deviation, with a bias toward the (cheaper) linear result when it is within the edge's precision and not much worse than the projected one. line_verification_notes: All V3 line citations for these five classes drift substantially from the verified V7_8_1 source (bd2a789f), and the drift grows through each file (roughly +15 to +30 lines early in ShapeAnalysis_Surface.cxx, growing to +100 to +150 lines by UVFromIso near the end), consistent with V3 having been built against a slightly different/expanded revision of these two large files. ShapeUpgrade_ConvertCurve2dToBezier.cxx and ShapeUpgrade_ConvertSurfaceToBezierBasis.cxx drift much less (0-90 lines). ShapeAnalysis_Curve.cxx drift is the most severe (up to ~260 lines) and V3 additionally left several whole functions as unlabeled '?' placeholder branches with no content at all (GetSamplePoints_at1262, GetSamplePoints_at1321, IsClosed_at1425, ShapeAnalysis_Surface.Singularity_at332, ShapeAnalysis_Surface.UVFromIso_at1523 [33 branches]) — all five were read directly from source to reconstruct their actual behavior and folded into tkshh-curve-adaptive-sample-density-and-zero-length-guard, tkshh-curve-tolerance-closure-detection, and tkshh-surface-uv-inversion-fallback-chain respectively (Singularity()'s two placeholder branches turned out to be a pure index-bounds accessor guard and were excluded, not kept). Two V3 branches were dropped outright as apparently mismatched/hallucinated against the verified source: ShapeAnalysis_Curve.NextProject.fallback_cast (claims a Bezier null-guard downcast that does not exist in NextProject) and ShapeAnalysis_Curve.SelectForwardSeam SEAM_001 (claims periodic-wrap deduplication logic that SelectForwardSeam does not implement — it is a pure direction/location heuristic). One additional genuine repair mechanism not really surfaced by V3's branch list was found by reading past the cited lines: ShapeUpgrade_ConvertSurfaceToBezierBasis.cxx:157-191's explicit thin-patch UReject/VReject filter (V3's bspline_split_insertion branch pointed elsewhere in the function); its exact debug string 'thin patches dropped' at line ~189 confirms the intent and was used as supporting evidence for tkshh-near-zero-knot-span-thin-patch-filter.
